news.title: CISA Flags Four Actively Exploited Flaws — Patch These Now
news.excerpt:
CISA just added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog — meaning attackers are actively using them right now. The flaws affect GPUStack (AI model server), SignalWire FreeSWITCH (VoIP), OpenBSD OpenSSH, and IBM Aspera Faspex (file transfer). If your computer runs any of these, update immediately.

What to do: Check for updates on every program you use. Turn on automatic updates in your system settings and in each application's settings. Most of these patches are already available from the vendors.

Why it matters: Actively exploited flaws are the ones criminals use first. Delaying updates leaves the door open.

news.title: Fake Windows 11 24H2 Update Scam Steals Data — Patch Tuesday Tomorrow
news.excerpt: A convincing fake Windows 11 24H2 update page is circulating. It mimics a Microsoft support site, uses a believable cumulative-update name, and offers a blue download button for an 83 MB installer. The file is a malicious MSI built with legitimate tools that hides an infostealer

news.title: ClickFix fake browser updates are tricking people into running malware — close the tab
news.excerpt: That "Update Chrome" or "Update Firefox" page that pops up while you're browsing? It's a lie. ClickFix scams mimic real browser updates to get you to copy-paste a malicious command into your terminal. Real browsers update themselves automatically — they never ask you to run commands. Close the tab. If it won't close, hold your power button for 15 seconds until the screen goes black, then turn it back on.

news.title: Scammers Are Faking Official-Looking Notices — Here's the Tell
news.excerpt:
Scammers Are Faking Official-Looking Notices — Here's the Tell.

You get an email or see a webpage that looks exactly like it's from
your bank, the IRS, or a government agency. The logo is perfect.
The formatting is perfect. It says "Immediate action required" and
threatens account closure, legal trouble, or lost benefits if you
don't respond today.

The giveaway: they ask for something no legitimate organization
would ever request by email. Your Social Security number. Your
bank login. A payment in gift cards or wire transfer. Remote access
to your computer.

Real banks and government agencies don't operate this way. They
already have your information. They don't threaten instant disaster.
They don't demand gift cards.

What to do: Don't click any links in the message. Don't call...

posts.title: CISA Flags Four Actively Exploited Flaws — GPUStack FreeSWITCH OpenSSH Aspera Faspex
posts.summary: CISA added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 9 2026 based on active exploitation. The flaws affect GPUStack (CVE-2026-102895) SignalWire FreeSWITCH (CVE-2026-116779) OpenBSD OpenSSH (CVE-2026-123158) and IBM Aspera Faspex (CVE-2026-123218). Organizations should prioritize patching these immediately. Check the catalog at cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog

posts.title: Microsoft Edge 157 Security Update Fixes Chromium Vulnerabilities — Update at edge://settings/help
posts.summary: Microsoft Edge 157 was released November 5 2026 as the Stable channel main release incorporating the latest Chromium security fixes. Update free by going to edge://settings/help or Settings > About Microsoft Edge. Automatic updates also apply if enabled.
posts.truth: Edge updates silently in the background for most people but I still see machines weeks behind on browser patches. Browser exploits are the number one way malware gets in — a single compromised website can hit an unpatched browser. Taking ten seconds to verify you're current is the highest-ROI security habit there is.

posts.title: Microsoft Fixes Windows 11 Black Screen After Sign In — KB5127648 Resolves Explorer Crash
posts.summary: Microsoft resolved a known issue where some Windows 11 devices show a black screen or fail to load the desktop after sign in caused by an Explorer crash. The fix is included in KB5127648 released October 13 2026 and all later cumulative updates. Install the latest Windows Update at Settings > Windows Update to get the fix.
posts.truth: This black screen bug scared a lot of customers — they thought their computer died. It's just Explorer crashing before the desktop loads. The fix has been out since mid-October but plenty of machines still haven't pulled it. If your screen goes black after login, you're not broken — you're just behind on updates.

posts.title: Firefox 160 Adds On-Device Speech Recognition in 40 Languages — Free Update at firefox.com
posts.summary: Firefox 160 was released November 10 2026 and includes on-device speech recognition using the Web Speech API for real-time speech-to-text conversion in 40 languages. Works on desktop offline with no cloud processing. Update free at firefox.com or open Settings > About Firefox to check for updates.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize their browser can now do speech-to-text locally without sending audio to Google or Microsoft. This is a genuine privacy win — your voice stays on your machine. I've been testing it and it's surprisingly accurate for dictating emails and documents.

posts.title: Chrome 157 Security Update Fixes 213 Bugs Including 7 Critical — Update at chrome://settings/help
posts.summary: Chrome 157 patches 213 security holes including seven critical flaws in graphics, memory handling, and browser features. Update now at chrome://settings/help — it takes two minutes and protects against memory corruption and graphics exploits.

posts.title: **Headline:** Microsoft Releases November Patch Tuesday Updates — Windows, Office, Edge
posts.summary: Microsoft released its November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates this afternoon covering Windows 11, Windows 10, Office, and Microsoft Edge. The updates address 78 security vulnerabilities across the product line including 6 rated Critical. Install via Settings > Windows Update and restart when prompted.
posts.truth: Patch Tuesday is the single most important day for computer security each month. Skipping updates leaves known vulnerabilities open. Most customers who bring in infected machines are months behind on patches.

posts.title: Windows 11 Built-In Troubleshooters Fix Common Problems Automatically — No Download Needed
posts.summary: Windows 11 includes free built-in troubleshooters that automatically diagnose and fix common problems like internet connections audio Windows Update printer issues and more. Run them at Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters. Select the troubleshooter for your issue and click Run.
posts.truth: People call for help with Wi-Fi that won't connect audio that's gone silent or updates that stall — and half the time the built-in troubleshooter fixes it before I even get to the machine. These tools have gotten genuinely good. They're not a magic wand but they're always worth trying first.

posts.title: DAILY BRIEF — Chrome 157 Patches 213 Flaws, CISA Flags SonicWall/Apple/WordPress
posts.summary: Chrome 157 fixes 213 security bugs including 7 critical — update at chrome://settings/help. CISA confirms three new actively exploited flaws: SonicWall SSLVPN, Apple authentication, WordPress core. Patch affected systems immediately.

posts.title: **Headline:** Stop renting Microsoft Office for $100 a year — LibreOffice is free and opens every Word Excel PowerPoint file
posts.summary: Download LibreOffice free at libreoffice.org. It includes Writer (Word), Calc (Excel), Impress (PowerPoint), Draw, Base, and Math. Opens and saves Microsoft Office formats. No subscription, no account needed.
posts.truth: LibreOffice opens and saves Microsoft Office formats (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). Free download at libreoffice.org, no subscription, no account needed.

posts.title: **Headline:** Windows Voice Typing (Win+H) types for you free — built into Windows 11
posts.summary: Press Win+H anywhere to dictate text — no install needed, works offline, handles punctuation commands like 'period' 'comma' 'new line'.
posts.truth: Windows has had solid dictation for years. Win+H is free, built into Windows 11, and already on the computer.
